name: Siôn Tudur
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Siôn Tudur (died 1602) was a Welsh poet of Wigfair near St Asaph, Denbighshire, who served for a time at the court in London and was made apprentice chief bard at the Caerwys eisteddfod of 1568. The Dictionary of Welsh Biography gives only his death date, 3 April 1602.
The poem here is George Borrow's English version, taken from his Wild Wales and printed in Welsh Poems and Ballads (1915).

poems.title: Chester Ale
poems.author: Siôn Tudur
poems.note: From "Wild Wales". Printed as "By Sion Tudor".
poems.translator: trans. George Borrow (Welsh Poems and Ballads, 1915)
poems.text:
CHESTER ale, Chester ale!  I could ne'er get it down,
   'Tis made of ground-ivy, of dirt, and of bran,
'Tis as thick as a river below a huge town!
   'Tis not lap for a dog, far less drink for a man.
